text:
sandeep: Quick sync — thinking about an async lease handshake for multi-region writes. Idea: allow local accept but escrow/forward to resident region in background when tenant residency = EU. Tradeoffs?

aj: Can we keep fast local reads + async writes? Concern: split-brain double-writes if partitioned.

maria: Legal note: if tenant has EU_residency=STRICT then we cannot let PII leave region, even transiently. That kills async forward unless escrowed within EU.

tim: Proposal: accept locally, return 200 immediately, enqueue a forward job that runs from resident-region-only workers. That keeps client latency but ensures data landing in region. Need to ensure local cache doesn't leak.

sandeep: Sketch of sequence:
```
client -> local-proxy -> local-store (accepted) -> return 200 + lease_token
background-job picks lease_token, forwards to resident-region -> resident-store ack -> local-store mark committed
if resident-store rejects -> mark conflict, surface to operator queue
```

aj: If resident-store unreachable, do we block acceptance? For STRICT, probably yes. For PREFERRED, allow enqueue.

maria: Suggest policy enum: STRICT | PREFERRED | ANY. STRICT = reject non-resident writes with 409 or 425 (retry later). PREFERRED = accept & enqueue but ensure queued work runs only on resident workers. ANY = default behavior.

legal-bot: Flagged - confirm that transient copies in ephemeral queue storage are covered by KMS/HSM and don't violate data export rules.

ops-bot: Telemetry asks: emit `async_replication_lag_p50/p95`, `queued_writes_count_by_tenant_region`, `failed_forwardings_total`. Add alert if p95 > 2s or queued_writes_count > 10000.

aj: Implementation note: proxy should attach header `X-Residence: eu` and `X-Escrow-Token`. Background forwarder must only run in eu region for STRICT tenants.

maria: Also need operator UI to inspect escrow queue per-tenant and ability to replay/abort. Audit logs must show where and when data was forwarded.

Tim: Conflict resolution: prefer deterministic CRDT-ish merge? Too heavy. Maybe version vector + reconciliation job that produces tombstones and operator diff.

aj: Prototype plan: small shim in proxy that 1) checks tenant residency, 2) for PREFERRED attaches header and returns 202, 3) for STRICT returns 409 and triggers client-facing error. I'll push PoC to `feature/async-lease-probe`.

sandeep: Open questions for RFC follow-up:
- exact semantics for return codes and retries (202 vs 200)
- escrow storage SLOs and encryption boundary
- conflict resolution primitive (LWW vs vector)
- operator surface & metrics

maria: I'll take legal gating and draft the policy mapping to country-specific requirements.

aj: I'll start the shim and wire `queued_writes_count` metric.

sandeep: OK assigning @aj for proxy prototype, @maria for policy gating, @tim for reconciliation design. Meeting Friday 10am to review PoC. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Meeting created: "Async lease probe - privacy & fallback" Fri 10:00.

aj: Quick note — POC will log `X-Escrow-Token` lifecycle, will redact tokens in telemetry.

maria: Thanks — please cc legal when you have the first design doc.

sandeep: Great work. We'll ship RFC v2 after PoC results.
